title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The neighbouring pages concern semi-simplicial ∂-perfect complexes in a k-linear category 𝒜, with a cochain object 𝒞^• = (𝒞^0 →d 𝒞^1 → …), duality L ↦ L^∨, and universal properties for E-exact functors into abelian categories ℬ (next page: Hom_{E-ex}(𝒫^•, ℬ), 'ℬ abélienne', 'adjoint'). This page is titled 'Construction canonique de 𝒫 (k-lin.)'. It asks for a k-linear category 𝒫 ⊃ 𝒜 satisfying three conditions.

(a) Corepresentability. The covariant functor L ↦ Hom(L,𝒞^0)^∨ (k-linear dual) should be corepresentable by an object Ψ^0, so that Hom(Ψ^0, L) ≅ Hom(L,𝒞^0)^∨ naturally in L. In modern terms Ψ^0 is the inverse Serre functor S^{-1} applied to 𝒞^0.
- The pairing Hom(𝒞^0,L) × Hom(L,𝒞^0) → End(𝒞^0) ≃ k, (u,v) ↦ vu, gives a natural map Hom(𝒞^0,L) → Hom(L,𝒞^0)^∨ ≅ Hom(Ψ^0,L).
- By Yoneda this is induced by a canonical morphism ε: Ψ^0 → 𝒞^0. It is the morphism corresponding to the linear form id-coefficient ('trace') on End(𝒞^0).

Check that ε is an augmentation. For u': 𝒞^1 → L put u = u'∘d^0. For any v: L → 𝒞^0 one has v∘u = (v∘u')∘d, and v∘u' ∈ Hom(𝒞^1,𝒞^0) is taken to be 0. Hence the composite Hom(𝒞^1,L) → Hom(𝒞^0,L) → Hom(Ψ^0,L) is zero for all L. By Yoneda, Ψ^0 → 𝒞^0 → 𝒞^1 is zero. So 𝒞^• is Ψ^0-augmented, and 𝒫^• denotes the augmented cochain complex Ψ^0 → 𝒞^0 → 𝒞^1 → ….

Then 𝒫_0 is defined as the k-linear subcategory of finite direct sums of objects of 𝒜 and copies of Ψ^0, i.e. objects L ⊕ (Ψ^0)^r with r ∈ ℕ and L ∈ Ob 𝒜. Earlier crossed-out versions ('family of 𝒞^i and Ψ^0 is strictly generating', '𝒫^• is a resolution of …') were replaced by the following.

(b) Relative exact structure. Σ is the class of sequences L' → L → L'' which every Hom(P,−), P ∈ 𝒫_0, turns into exact sequences 0 → Hom(P,L') → Hom(P,L) → Hom(P,L'') → 0. This is the relative exact structure (projective class) determined by 𝒫_0.

(c) Resolution condition. The augmented complex (𝒞^•, Ψ^0, ε) should be a Σ-resolution, i.e. 𝒫^• is Σ-acyclic: Hom(P,−) of it is exact for all P ∈ 𝒫_0.

Purpose. Freely adjoin to 𝒜 an object Ψ^0 dual to 𝒞^0 (Serre-dual/Auslander–Reiten-type) so that 𝒞^• becomes a relative-projective resolution of Ψ^0. On the next page this feeds a universal property: Σ-exact functors from 𝒫 into abelian categories ℬ correspond to suitable data on 𝒜. This looks like a step towards a 'universal' or 'dévissage' category for ∂-perfect complexes.
errors: The key step v∘u' = 0 uses Hom(𝒞^1,𝒞^0) = 0. This is not stated on the page; it is presumably a hypothesis from the semi-simplicial setting (no backward maps), but it is a gap as written.
End(𝒞^0) ≃ k is an assumption: 𝒞^0 must be 'simple' in a strong sense, or else one needs a chosen linear form (trace) on End(𝒞^0) to build the pairing.
Notational slip: 'w∘u' is written where 'v∘u' is meant.
'Est représentable' for a covariant functor means corepresentable: Hom(Ψ^0,−). The text uses it correctly in that sense.
Condition (b) is defined via 𝒫_0, while condition (c) is a constraint on 𝒫, so the construction is still only a list of requirements here. Existence and canonicity of 𝒫 are not proved on this page.

ideas.what: Adjoin an object Ψ^0 corepresenting L ↦ Hom(L,𝒞^0)^∨, with canonical map Ψ^0 → 𝒞^0 induced by the composition pairing into End(𝒞^0) ≃ k
ideas.modern_name: Inverse Serre functor / Auslander–Reiten-type duality object, S^{-1}(𝒞^0)
ideas.where_published: Duality via a trace pairing is pervasive in SGA4/SGA5 Grothendieck duality, but not in this categorical form.

ideas.what: Yoneda argument that Ψ^0 augments the complex 𝒞^• using Hom(𝒞^1,𝒞^0) = 0
Class Σ of sequences made short exact by Hom(P,−) for P in a chosen subcategory 𝒫_0, with Σ-resolutions and Σ-acyclicity
ideas.modern_name: Relative homological algebra / projective classes / exact structure induced by a subcategory

ideas.what: Building a canonical k-linear category 𝒫 ⊃ 𝒜 with a universal property for Σ-exact functors to abelian categories (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Free / universal exact or abelian envelope of a linear category with prescribed resolutions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Freyd (free abelian category, 1966); later work on abelian envelopes (e.g. Coulembier, Entova–Hinich–Serganova)

missed.claim: Grothendieck uses an inverse-Serre-type object, Hom(Ψ^0,L) ≅ Hom(L,𝒞^0)^∨, with a trace-induced map Ψ^0 → 𝒞^0, to turn a cochain complex into a relative-projective resolution. This is a Serre-functor / Auslander–Reiten-flavoured construction inside a universal-property problem for exact functors, in 1975–76, independently of the Auslander–Reiten school.
missed.quote: Le foncteur covariant L ↦ Hom(L,𝒞^0)^∨ est représentable par un objet Ψ^0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It shows Grothendieck using Serre-functor duality as a categorical tool for constructing universal exact/abelian envelopes. That combination appears explicitly in the literature only much later (Bondal–Kapranov, tensor/abelian envelopes). The page is fragmentary, though.

missed.claim: The canonical construction of 𝒫 (existence, and the universal property for Σ-exact functors to abelian ℬ) is only set up as a list of conditions with several crossed-out attempts. No proof or completion is visible on this page.
missed.quote: Le complexe augmenté (𝒞^•, Ψ^0, ε) est une Σ-résolution, i.e. 𝒫^• est Σ-acyclique
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could be read as a precursor to universal constructions for linear categories with prescribed resolutions, but only modestly so.

deep.surprise_reason: Mostly standard relative homological algebra plus a Yoneda argument. The Serre-dual adjoined object is a mildly interesting, unpublished design choice, but the material is fragmentary and close to known techniques.
transcription_corrections: 'Construction canonique de 𝒫 (h-lin)' should read '(k-lin.)', i.e. k-linéaire; likewise 'h-lin.' later.
'L⊗(Ψ^0)^r' is almost certainly 'L ⊕ (Ψ^0)^r' (finite sums of objects of 𝒜 and copies of Ψ^0).
Margin note reads roughly 'foncteur Ψ^0 ↦ Hom(𝒫^?,L)', placement uncertain.
'Ψ^0_0' in 'objets de la forme 𝒞^i, Ψ^0_0' is likely just 'Ψ^0'.
